svg.title: Parallax of a nearby star
svg.desc: A star 4 light years from the Sun, far above the plane of the Earth’s orbit (not to scale). From the Earth at opposite sides of its orbit, six months apart, the lines of sight to the star make angles θ1 and θ2 with the line through the Sun. The known diameter of the orbit and these angles fix the distance to the star. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Earth’s annual motion changes the apparent direction to a nearby star
A star at 2 pc has parallax p ≈ 0.5 arcsec. The orbit is drawn in perspective; distance and angles
are enlarged. Parallax p is the half-angle; opposite extremes differ by about 2p.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
